hot.title: Embodied First Exam
hot.summary: The Embodied First Exam (EFE) evaluates coding agents controlling robots across direct control, controller-writing, and policy-training approaches. It standardizes tasks, information access, resources, and external verification across 1,156 tasks, 35 suites, and 47 robots. On 391 paired core tasks, GPT-6 Astra solved 30% in Standard and 77% in Privileged; these simulated results compare access conditions, not real-world readiness.

hot.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
hot.summary: The authors present Sage-Taiyi, a research system that tracks evidence, assumptions, uncertainty, and scope to guide which targets and reasoning methods to pursue. In expert-guided cobalt-catalyzed carbonylation, condition optimization raised isolated yield from trace to 84%. On Taiyi-Bench, Sage-Taiyi scored 53.95 versus 47.85 for AI Scientist-v2; this full-system comparison does not isolate monitoring’s contribution.

hot.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
hot.summary: Agency inserts an interposition layer between harnesses, models, and tools to reduce context and calls. Its techniques compact context, remove stale history, search metadata, and batch calls. Across 200 tasks, four models, and three harnesses, they average 0.77 of baseline cost and 0.97 of baseline accuracy, though some tasks cost more and accuracy declines on some OfficeQA tasks.

hot.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
hot.summary: Evolving Infra separates node phase allocation from shared KV-cache management, allowing nodes to switch between prefill and decode while cached context remains accessible. An online planner adapts the split, and a branch-aware directory guides cache eviction. On tested workloads, it reduced mean request latency, though Putnam P95 TTFT sometimes exceeded Dynamo’s.

hot.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
hot.summary: The authors introduce LingBot-Touch, which maps different tactile sensors’ readings into a shared representation of contact that robot policies can reuse. Its frozen encoder supplies features alongside policy inputs. Across 26 real-robot tasks, adding these features to LingBot-VLA raises mean success from 48.3% to 73.1%, versus 56.5% with raw touch; gains are not universal, and evaluation covers two hands and fingertip-focused data.

hot.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
hot.summary: The authors survey mechanistic interpretability as a way to study models’ internal representations and computations, using causal interventions to test explanations. They propose evaluating analyses for attribution faithfulness, completeness, stability, causal validity, and human interpretability. In a constructed sleeper-agent model, a linear probe decoded trigger state with >99% AUROC, demonstrating decodability, not causal understanding or a safety guarantee.

hot.title: Speculative Self-Distillation enables Efficient Knowledge Internalization
hot.summary: The paper introduces selective self-distillation (SSD), training a model to answer using context-informed teacher guidance. SSD uses the teacher’s next token when its prediction differs from the student’s beyond a threshold, while applying distillation loss at every response position. Across three QA tasks, it uses 38–69% fewer supervised tokens than on-policy training, with accuracy within 1.4 percentage points except on Company Memo.

hot.title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
hot.summary: Evolving Infra adapts prefill–decode allocation for agent workloads while keeping KV cache state available across nodes as roles change. Its planner estimates phase workloads, while routing and eviction manage reusable cache. On a shifting Kimi K2.6 workload, mean end-to-end request latency was 38.7 seconds, versus 83.1 with Dynamo. P95 TTFT rose above Dynamo on decode-heavy Putnam at two tested concurrency levels.

hot.title: UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model
hot.summary: UGG unifies video generation and geometric prediction by completing aligned RGB, depth, and camera-ray representations from observed scene components. A shared multimodal model treats observed tokens as context and denoises missing ones; test-time search ranks candidate completions using image-derived evidence. On RealEstate10K with only endpoint images, search lowers translation-direction angular error from 8.260° to 3.475°, but verification is imperfect.

hot.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
hot.summary: APEX adapts condition shifting to streaming video generation, using the same model for generation and fake-distribution estimation by negating the projected text condition. It retains the frozen teacher and S2-Avatar’s replay training. In matched training settings, iteration time fell 9.2% and peak memory 4.4%; instruction-following preference improved, but motion preference favored S2-Avatar and benchmark quality was mixed.

hot.title: Blind Variation, Selective Retention: Improving Creative Idea Generation in AI Scientists
hot.summary: BVSR reduces task-specific information during idea generation and uses outcomes from tested proposals to screen candidates before verification. At a 50% discard rate, it retains 79% of top-5% proposals by creativity and 82% by utility, separately. In SimpleTES, BVSR reaches higher final scores on all five evaluated tasks with fewer verified proposals; this does not establish elapsed-time savings.

hot.title: The Minimum Canonical Volume of Threefolds of General Type
hot.summary: The authors prove that smooth complex projective threefolds of general type have canonical volume at least 1/420. They use restrictions of holomorphic two-forms to divisors and whole pluricanonical members, plus numerical tests, to exclude the remaining cases with Euler characteristics two and three. A smooth model of a general degree-46 hypersurface in P(4,5,6,7,23) attains the bound.

hot.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
hot.summary: RoboScript lets a frozen model learn manipulation tasks by rehearsing from one demonstration in simulation and recording task steps, object roles, and relative geometry in text memory without updating its weights. On RoboTwin 2.0’s 50 dual-arm tasks, GPT-6.1-Sol achieves 83.4% mean success, versus 61.7% for 4D-WAM, after clean-only rehearsal; this result is limited to the benchmark and protocol.

hot.title: Review the Episodes, Refine the Lessons: Simple Memory Evolution for Embodied Agents
hot.summary: SimplEvo lets embodied agents retain task guidance and lessons from their attempts in two text memories, without changing model weights or delegating execution to a controller. Memories are learned during training and fixed at test time. In simulation, success rate reaches 81.7% on EBench, up from 46.7% under direct control; evidence is limited to two simulated benchmarks, not physical robots.

hot.title: WorkflowArena: Benchmarking Executable Workflow Orchestration in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
hot.summary: WorkflowArena evaluates how models organize long-horizon tasks by choosing whether and how to delegate, recording workflows alongside deliverables across 145 tasks in eight domains. In a fixed-executor transfer test, Kimi scores 45.04 with static workflows authored by Opus and 29.69 with those authored by Astra. Overall Resolved peaks at 36.95%, an equal-weight domain average; no configuration leads every domain.

hot.title: Compass 1: Towards Open-World and Persistent Embodied Navigation from Monocular RGB Videos
hot.summary: Compass 1 helps robots return to landmarks encountered earlier during navigation. It selects sparse past views and organizes their positions and headings in a map, then uses questions to identify which earlier view contains a requested target and which way to travel. On the tested real-world persistent-history-backtracking task, it succeeds in 58% of trials, while the strongest baseline scores 0%.

hot.title: Ego Guidance: Enhancing Robot Policy Learning with Action-Free Human Egocentric Videos
hot.summary: Ego Guidance trains a vision-language backbone with robot-action prediction and future-image-feature prediction, letting human videos without action labels shape its representation. On LIBERO-Plus, SigLIP2 features achieve 76.2% average success across seven shift dimensions, versus 60.0% for Wan-VAE latents. OOD success rises with more Open-AoE video, while in-domain success changes little; raw video underperforms robot-only, showing benefits depend on curation.

hot.title: SWAM: Scaling World Action Models with Cross-Modal Alignment
hot.summary: SWAM jointly predicts future video and robot actions conditioned on language, retaining video prediction while learning actions. Its video and action branches share masked attention. Across cup stacking, towel folding, and gift-in-box under real-world Hard conditions, SWAM's equally weighted mean complete-task success rate is 40.00%, versus 23.33% for OpenWAM; the result is limited to these three tasks and conditions.

hot.title: Are UFOs Real? Introducing Unified Factored Organizers
hot.summary: The authors introduce a learned auxiliary autoencoder that reconstructs a primary network’s internal activations, while training encourages those activations to be reconstructible. This adds a learned representation constraint alongside task loss. In a small transformer trained on division modulo 97, selective regularization reached 99% held-out accuracy at a median 8,000 steps, versus 98,000 for weight decay alone; this is a step-count comparison in one task, not compute.

hot.title: LaST0.5: A Generalist World Action Model with Interaction-Centric Latent Reasoning
hot.summary: LaST₀.₅ adds an interaction-focused latent representation between predicted scene dynamics and action generation, using motion and target-object affordance cues during training. Its adaptive executor uses predicted task progress to decide whether to continue an action chunk or replan. It reports 99.5% across four LIBERO’s suites and 88% across ten RLBench tasks, averages that do not imply success on every task.

likes.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
likes.summary: FrontierPhysics evaluates whether AI agents can conduct open-ended physics research from high-level briefs. The benchmark uses physicist-contributed research tasks and grades structured outputs with deterministic checks, alongside manuscripts and research trajectories against expert-authored rubrics. Passing requires all verifier tests and blocking criteria. The top tested configuration passed 46/168 trials (27.4%), measuring performance under this protocol rather than human publication acceptance.

likes.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
likes.summary: VFlash generates spatial plans for vision-language models by drafting complete structured primitives, such as trajectories, in parallel, while retaining target-verified decoding for text. On MolmoSpaces, a world action model using VFlash plans reaches 70.2% success versus 61.0% with autoregressive plans. On Jetson Thor, batch-one model-pipeline latency is 703.3 ms versus 3,552.7 ms; this is not full robot response time.

likes.title: A Survey on Continuous Diffusion and Flow Language Models
likes.summary: The authors survey continuous language models for parallel, few-step text generation, explaining how shared sequence flows couple token positions and how learned flow maps make finite jumps. They contrast this with independent marginal sampling and discuss RePlaid’s training-compute gap: 20× with self-conditioning, down from Plaid’s 64×. Scaling matched discrete diffusion over the evaluated compute range; practical efficiency remains open.

likes.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
likes.summary: SwarmEvolve uses many agents to search for scientific and mathematical programs, sharing internal model memories instead of lengthy text. A synthesizer writes candidate programs, which an evaluator scores. Across 21 problems, Qwen3 8B averaged 0.804, versus CodeEvolve’s 0.700, in 60-minute runs. Its median time to reach OpenEvolve’s 60-minute score was 7 minutes, a time-to-target result, not a universal win.

likes.title: Introducing Inkling 2 Small
likes.summary: Inkling 2 Small is Thinking Machines Lab's second model generation: a 594B-total, 17B-active Mixture-of-Experts model with a 292M-parameter vision encoder and variable effort. It scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, launching on Tinker with closed weights ahead of a planned Apache 2.0 weight release after external safety testing. The post covers its coding, autoresearch, vision, knowledge work and alignment results alongside details of its pretraining and a single joint RL run.

likes.title: FlashStates: Unlocking Flexible Hybrid State Management for Agentic LLM Inference
likes.summary: FlashStates improves prefix reuse for hybrid language models, which require both attention key-value tensors and a recurrent checkpoint at the same prefix endpoint. Arbitrary State Checkpointing captures that complete state at request endpoints, while a cost-aware policy jointly admits and evicts states. On GLM-5.3-Flash, it delivers 4.66 million prefill tokens per minute per GPU, 3.14× vLLM, in coding-agent trace replays on three hybrid models, not a universal serving guarantee.

likes.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
likes.summary: Scientist World turns empirical AI research papers into runnable environments where agents reproduce methods, set improvement targets, package tasks, and verify them. Its release contains 1,000 environments, while tests cover ten lower-compute environments. Attempts improved over reproduced methods in 84% of Improve runs and 74% of Innovate runs, measured by held-out gains; Innovate has more regressions.

likes.title: SLA: Scaling Spatial-Language-Action Model via Continual Pre-training
likes.summary: SLA teaches a vision-language-action policy spatial structure by aligning its intermediate visual features with a frozen 3D perception model during continual pre-training and task-specific post-training, without adding depth as a policy input. On RoboTwin 2.0 Clean2Random, both-stage alignment reaches 72.3% success, above either single-stage alternative; this result supports the combined recipe in the tested setup, not universal causation.

likes.title: From Pixels to Actions--Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
likes.summary: NEO-VLA processes pixels and instruction words in one backbone, allowing a continuous-action expert to read representations from selected layers. In LIBERO, distributed access across the 40-layer backbone averages 90.9% success with the backbone frozen, versus 86.7% for final-layer access; after fine-tuning it reaches 95.3%. Real-world performance remains limited, with 17 successes in 20 trials on one task.

likes.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
likes.summary: HALO trains a humanoid robot to turn language requests and camera views into whole-body actions. It uses simulated homes to generate paired vision-language-motion examples while people still author task prompts and motion keyframes. In six unseen, unmapped real-world homes, it achieves 91% mean success across six tested single-task skills, not longer sequences. Its stack combines planning, generation, and tracking.

likes.title: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations
likes.summary: The authors introduce Mechanistic Shaping, which uses internal representations to penalize a model’s reliance on specified concepts or their expression. In a constructed, perfectly drain-confounded pneumothorax benchmark, reliance shaping raises worst-group accuracy from 33.3% with ordinary training to 61.3%, above the 56.0% group-balanced reference. This result concerns a 100-patient test, not clinical deployment; concepts may remain encoded.

likes.title: Learning Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation
likes.summary: On-policy distillation trains a language-model student on its own continuations using a teacher’s token-level feedback. The authors trace how feedback changes parameters and predictions, and how those changes redirect training prefixes. A larger teacher transfers less than a smaller RL-trained sibling: the same 1.5B student reaches AIME accuracy of 0.31 versus 0.45. Findings are limited to models and settings tested.

likes.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
likes.summary: The authors evaluate critic-guided reinforcement learning for improving a generalist robot policy across simulated manipulation tasks. The methods learn from experience across varied tasks and use action-value estimates to guide action selection or policy updates. In MolmoSpaces, gains reach 58 percentage points on unseen scenes and 39 on unseen objects, but are maxima in tested settings, not arbitrary-task generalization.

likes.title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
likes.summary: Open-HumanWAM uses curated human video and aligned hand-motion labels to pretrain a model that predicts future video and actions, then adapts it with robot demonstrations. In RoboTwin 2.0, after robot post-training, Scene-OOD success rises from 49.1% with 100 hours of human pretraining to 73.2% with 50,000 hours. Clean success changes little; these are empirical results on tested benchmarks.

likes.title: Embodied First Exam
likes.summary: The Embodied First Exam (EFE) evaluates coding agents controlling robots across direct control, controller-writing, and policy-training approaches. It standardizes tasks, information access, resources, and external verification across 1,156 tasks, 35 suites, and 47 robots. On 391 paired core tasks, GPT-6 Astra solved 30% in Standard and 77% in Privileged; these simulated results compare access conditions, not real-world readiness.

likes.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
likes.summary: SINKSTATE reduces recurrent-state traffic during linear-attention decoding by maintaining an adaptive low-rank representation. It buffers token updates, applies local SVD updates, and asynchronously consolidates frozen components on the CPU. In evaluation on four Mamba-2/GDN models, Nemotron-3-Nano-4B achieved 1.58× speedup on MATH-500, while peak recurrent-state memory averaged 0.52 of dense baselines and benchmark accuracy changed without a consistent loss.

likes.title: La-JEPA: Compact Robot Policies with Latent World Modeling
likes.summary: La-JEPA trains compact robot-control transformers from scratch using pretrained V-JEPA 2.1 visual features, predicting future features alongside actions during training but generating only actions at inference. On corrected-instruction LIBERO-Plus, La-JEPA L reaches 88.0% success versus NowWAM’s 86.2%, with 1.78B versus 7.1B deployed parameters. La-JEPA B averages 60.8% on clean-trained RoboTwin, but remains below strongest embodied-pretrained methods on randomized scenes.
